properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD — OPTION A: ALL TWENTY SERVED SKILLS GET A SLASH COMMAND, AND THE COVERAGE IS PINNED BY A TEST.**

Raised the same day after `/capture-session` came back `Unknown command` on his work computer. At the time nine of twenty skills were fronted by a command and eleven by nothing.

He was given three options and took A over B (fix discovery instead) and C (cover only what people type by name). **TWO THINGS MOVED THE ARGUMENT, and both are dated later than the reasoning that originally held the set at eight:**

1. **THE CLUTTER OBJECTION HAD ALREADY BEEN PAID DOWN.** The case against widening was Alex's *"inserted several things into my project"*, which is why `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` narrowed the install. But that shipped in PR #178 on 2026-08-14: `init` now ASKS which harness and writes `.claude/commands` for Claude Code ONLY. An OpenCode or VS Code project receives none of them, so the cost that argued against twenty files is no longer paid by the projects that complained.

2. **MEASURED THE SAME DAY — COMMANDS ARE THE CHANNEL THAT ACTUALLY GETS USED.** `fact:skill-use-measured-two-channels-2026-08-14`: across every retained transcript, `where-am-i` was invoked **37 times as `/where` against 4 `get_skill` calls**. 55 of 63 sessions invoked a skill by command or Skill tool; 35 used `get_skill`. People type shortcuts; they rarely instruct an agent to fetch a skill. **A skill with no command is reachable only by the weaker of the two channels.**

⭐ **AND THE MEASUREMENT CUTS BOTH WAYS, WHICH IS WHY THE TEST IS PART OF THE RULING.** A skill WITH a command is invoked locally and vanishes from `get_skill` counts; a skill WITHOUT one can arrive by no other route. So widening coverage will make `surface_usage.py` report LOWER apparent skill use unless it learns to count both channels. That is a measurement artefact, not a regression, and it must not be read as one.

═══ WHAT IS OWED, AND THE SECOND HALF IS THE DURABLE ONE ═══

· Eleven new command files for capture-session, ci-gate, impact-check, ingest-corpus, link-artifacts, link-projects, parallel-work, plan-increments, report-friction, retire-from-design, revise-design.
· **A TEST THAT PINS COVERAGE.** `skill_lint` already fails a command naming a skill that does not exist; **nothing fails a skill that no command names**, and nothing pins the count — which is how `dec:commands-are-the-exception`, `chg:commands-ship` and `ver:install-reaches-the-agent` all still say EIGHT while eleven ship. Without this half the set silently falls behind again the next time a skill is added.
· The three records above should be corrected to the shipped number rather than left saying eight.
properties.name: OPEN — does every served skill get a slash command, or is the shortfall the wrong thing to fix?
properties.rationale:
THE OPTIONS, WITH WHAT EACH COSTS. None is recommended here; the measurement is the contribution.

**A — ship all twenty.** Consistent, and it is the option `dec:commands-are-the-exception` already argues for: each command is four lines of pointer with no version-coupled content, so twenty rot no faster than eight. COST: twenty files in a consumer repo. Alex, 2026-08-14, on init: it *"inserted several things into my project"* — and that report is why `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` narrowed the install. **Widening the command set runs directly against the complaint that was just settled**, and these are Claude-Code-only files, so an OpenCode project gets twenty it cannot read.

**B — ship none of the missing eleven, and fix DISCOVERY instead.** The server instructions already list every skill; the failure is that a user reaches for `/name` and gets a flat `Unknown command` from the HARNESS, which reflow2 never sees and cannot answer. COST: does nothing for the person typing the slash. Nothing in reflow2 can intercept it.

**C — cover the skills a user REACHES FOR by name, and say so.** capture-session is the demonstrated case. COST: the criterion is taste, and the current eleven were chosen by the same unstated taste — which is how the shortfall went unnoticed.

**WHAT IS NOT OPTIONAL EITHER WAY, and is the cheaper half:** the guard is asymmetric. `skill_lint` fails a command naming a missing skill; **nothing fails a skill that no command names**, and nothing pins the count, so the record still says "eight" while eleven ship. Whichever option wins, the intended coverage should be asserted somewhere a test can read it — otherwise the next skill ships uncovered in silence exactly as these eleven did.

**THE STANDING TRAP:** this is invisible from inside the checkout. `.claude/skills/` holds all twenty as compile sources, so Claude Code resolves every skill as `/name` HERE and on no consumer install. Any judgement about command ergonomics made in this repo is made in the one environment where the shortfall does not exist.
